identity.title: POCUS lung: >=3 B-lines per intercostal space in >=2 bilateral zones (interstitial syndrome)

technique.how: Curvilinear or phased-array probe, longitudinal, scanning 4 anterior/lateral zones per hemithorax (8-zone protocol) or the BLUE points. In each interspace count vertical, laser-like, pleura-to-bottom artifacts that move with sliding and erase A-lines; a positive zone has >=3 B-lines, and a positive study has >=2 positive zones bilaterally.
technique.prerequisites: Patient supine or semi-recumbent; operator trained in lung POCUS; interpret with cardiac POCUS, IVC and clinical context.

interpretation.positive_finding: Bilateral, diffuse, symmetric B-lines (>=3 per space in >=2 zones each side) with sliding preserved: interstitial syndrome, most often cardiogenic pulmonary edema in a dyspneic patient.
interpretation.negative_finding: A-line predominance bilaterally (no B-line zones) makes cardiogenic pulmonary edema unlikely (pooled sensitivity around 0.88-0.94) and points to COPD/asthma, PE or other causes.
interpretation.pitfalls: B-lines are non-specific: pneumonia, ARDS, interstitial lung disease, fibrosis and volume overload without heart failure (dialysis patients) also produce them; focal or asymmetric B-lines suggest pneumonia rather than edema. Accuracy depends on zone count, threshold and operator.
interpretation.changes_what: Bilateral B-lines in acute dyspnea: treat as cardiogenic edema/volume overload pending BNP/echo; A-profile shifts the workup toward COPD/asthma or PE.

estimates.target_condition: Acute decompensated heart failure (cardiogenic pulmonary edema) by LUS B-lines
estimates.population: Adults presenting with dyspnea; 6 prospective studies, 1,827 patients (4 ED, 2 internal-medicine ward cohorts); Volpicelli criteria (>=3 B-lines in >=2 zones bilaterally) or modification; 1 to >=12 operators per study
estimates.reference_standard: ADHF diagnosis by expert medical record review (5 studies) or echocardiography + BNP + CXR criteria (1 study)
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.88/(1-0.90) = 8.8; LR- = (1-0.88)/0.90 = 0.13, from pooled sensitivity 0.88 and specificity 0.90
estimates.quote: Pooled estimates for LUS were 0.88 (95% Cl, 0.75-0.95) for sensitivity and 0.90 (95% Cl, 0.88-0.92) for specificity.

estimates.target_condition: Acute cardiogenic pulmonary edema by B-lines
estimates.population: Patients presenting with acute dyspnea or suspected CHF; 7 prospective studies, n=1,075 (2 ED, 2 ICU, 2 ward, 1 prehospital)
estimates.quote: sensitivity of US using B-lines to diagnosis ACPE is 94.1% (95% confidence interval [CI] = 81.3% to 98.3%) and the specificity is 92.4%

estimates.target_condition: Pulmonary edema (BLUE B-profile: multiple anterior diffuse B-lines with lung sliding)
estimates.population: 260 consecutive ICU admissions with acute respiratory failure and definite diagnosis; 64 pulmonary edema; single expert operator
estimates.quote: Multiple anterior diffuse B lines with lung sliding indicated pulmonary edema (n=64) with 97% sensitivity and 95% specificity.

sources.citation: Maw AM, Hassanin A, Ho PM, et al. Diagnostic accuracy of point-of-care lung ultrasonography and chest radiography in adults with symptoms suggestive of acute decompensated heart failure: a systematic review and meta-analysis. JAMA Netw Open. 2019;2(3):e190703.

Al Deeb M, Barbic S, Featherstone R, Dankoff J, Barbic D. Point-of-care ultrasonography for the diagnosis of acute cardiogenic pulmonary edema in patients presenting with acute dyspnea: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Acad Emerg Med. 2014;21(8):843-852.
Lichtenstein DA, Meziere GA. Relevance of lung ultrasound in the diagnosis of acute respiratory failure: the BLUE protocol. Chest. 2008;134(1):117-125.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not attribute B-lines to heart failure without corroborating cardiac POCUS/clinical data in patients with known ILD, ARDS, pneumonia or on dialysis; do not use a single-zone scan.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Diffuse B-lines with hypotension or poor LV function on cardiac POCUS suggests cardiogenic shock; escalate and avoid fluid boluses.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Maw 2019: interrater kappa for LUS in 3 studies ranged 0.70-1.00 (Results, Study Characteristics); Al Deeb 2014 subgroup analyses by protocol did not significantly change pooled estimates.
safety_scope.skill_assumption: Assumes an operator trained in lung POCUS who can identify the pleural line, distinguish B-lines from Z-lines/comet tails, apply a multi-zone protocol and the >=3 B-lines/>=2 zones bilateral threshold; included studies used a mix of novices with brief training and experts.

extraction_notes: Primary estimate is the Maw 2019 HSROC pooled sensitivity/specificity, verified in the PMC full text Results paragraph; LRs computed from the pooled point estimates and flagged computed. Threshold/protocol details (Volpicelli criteria, 4-12 zones, kappa 0.70-1.00) taken from Maw Table 2 and Results text. Al Deeb 2014 (not open access) numbers from abstract; quote truncated to 25 words so the specificity CI (84.2-96.4%) appears in the estimate fields only. BLUE B-profile from Lichtenstein 2008 abstract; prevalence not entered because uncertain/rare diagnoses were excluded from the denominator.
